Subject: Time-to-first-token & streaming behavior — Opal Systems post-demo review

Hi Nadia,

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Per our conversation I wanted to capture the performance targets and the test plan so we have aligned next steps. High-level asks from your side:

- Time-to-first-token (median): target ~120–180 ms for median TTFT under typical 1–3k token prompts.
- TTFT 95th percentile: no more than ~420 ms during normal traffic; acceptable fallback up to 650 ms during bursts.
- Streaming protocol: Opal prefers WebSocket for your browser clients; SSE is acceptable for server-to-server.
- Chunking / payload cadence: you want small payload frames so front-end can render progressively — roughly 150–300 ms between chunks is ideal.
- Concurrency & throughput: estimate target concurrency of 80–120 concurrent streams during peak for initial rollout; burst tolerance to 250 concurrent connections.

Next steps we proposed on the call:
1) Opal to share a small representative traffic dump (token counts, sequence lengths, typical prompt templates) — we requested the spreadsheet attached (opalsystems_mtp_data_request.xlsx).
2) Redwood to run a focused TTFT + streaming probe against a dedicated test instance and share histograms across median/95/99 pctl.
3) Engineering deep-dive to validate WebSocket handshake performance and chunkization behavior — suggested slot: next Tue (9/14) 11:00am PT.

We will also include a short checklist for integration items (attached: redwood-streaming-checklist.pdf). Ben and Karthik will own the technical run.

If the above captures things correctly, confirm and we'll schedule the tech-call invite.

Best,

Sergio,

Thanks — this is helpful and captures our priorities. A couple clarifications from our platform team:

- The 120–180 ms median is our internal UX bar for the desktop web client. Mobile tends to be ~25% slower; we'll call out mobile separately if that matters for the probe.
- For 95th pctl we are comfortable with up to 500 ms during normal ops if the median stays tight, but would like the 99th pctl not to exceed 1s except for rare infra events.
- WebSocket is preferred for client-side streaming because we need duplex control messages. We will accept SSE for server-side integrations.
- Chunk size: our renderer expects < 3KB chunks for immediate rendering; larger deltas are okay if they arrive in the 200–300 ms window.
- Security: platform@opalsystems.com will need an encryption-at-rest confirmation and a short SOC-2 artifact list — can your team include that in the tech-call?

We attached an exported example of 500 recent prompts (anonymized) — see the attached worksheet column "prompt_length_tokens". We'll upload the full dataset to the Drive link you shared.

Confirming the tech call Tuesday 9/14 11am PT works.

Thanks,
Nadia
Head of Product / Opal Systems

Hi Nadia — copying the proposed technical plan so we have an explicit test sequence before Tue's call.

Planned probe (Redwood technical run):
- Environment: dedicated test instance using r-inference:open-12b (quantized) in us-west-2.
- Load shape: replay of 500 anonymized prompts provided by Opal at scaled QPS to emulate 100 concurrent streams for 5 minutes, then burst to 250 concurrent for 2 minutes.
- Observables: TTFT latency (median, p95, p99), token throughput (tokens/sec), chunk inter-arrival distribution, websocket handshake time, tail latency during bursts.
- Chunking: we'll run two experiments: 1) server-side chunking to ~2KB frames targeting 200ms cadence; 2) larger chunking (5–8KB) to measure render tradeoffs.
- Fallbacks: test graceful fallback to a smaller model variant and to SSE mode to measure delta in TTFT.

Data we will deliver: per-request trace IDs, latency histograms in CSV, and a short analysis doc with recommendations (quantization, batching changes, and suggested target concurrency headroom).

Security artifacts: Karthik will include a short note on encryption-at-rest and where SOC-2 evidence lives; we'll attach the minimal artifact list for platform to review prior to the tech call.

Action items:
- Nadia/Opal: upload the anonymized prompt dump to the Drive folder and confirm mobile vs desktop split if you want separate probes (deadline: EOD Mon 9/13).
- Ben/Karthik: provision test instance and smoke-run baseline by EOD Mon 9/13.
- Sergio: send calendar invite for Tue 9/14 11am PT (done).

Will post results in the Drive link and ping when the CSVs are available.
